column3: The Hebrew says it was found written; BSB makes the readers the subject of finding a passage.
The Hebrew switches to a singular subject hiring Balaam against a singular referent; BSB uses plural subjects and objects.
The Hebrew calls those separated a mixed company; BSB describes everyone of foreign descent.
The Hebrew names a chamber in the singular; BSB refers to storerooms.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he came to the king and asked leave after some days; BSB says he returned to Artaxerxes and obtained leave.
The Hebrew begins a separate statement that he came to Jerusalem; BSB attaches returning there to his leave.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he commanded, they purified the chambers, and he brought the articles back; BSB uses orders and arrangements for both actions.
The Hebrew says each fled to his field; BSB says they had gone back to their own fields.
The Hebrew says he gathered them; BSB explicitly identifies them as the Levites and singers.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says distribution to their brothers; BSB specifies their fellow Levites.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they brought the loads and he warned them on the day they sold food; BSB uses passive transport and a warning against selling on that day.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they add wrath upon Israel; BSB says they are rekindling His wrath.
The Hebrew says the gates grew dark and that they should not open the doors; BSB describes evening shadows and uses a passive prohibition.
The Hebrew says once and twice; BSB says once or twice.
The Hebrew has a singular hand and says they did not come on the Sabbath; BSB uses hands and says they did not return.
The Hebrew includes coming before guarding the gates; BSB omits this separate action.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls them sons and describes the language of one people and another; BSB uses children and rearranges the language descriptions.
The Hebrew says he plucked them and made them swear by God; BSB specifies hair and says before God.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew asks whether to listen to them to do all this great evil; BSB asks whether it must be heard that they are doing it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the noun for defilements of the priesthood; BSB turns this into an active statement that they defiled it.
The Hebrew says he purified them; BSB names the priests and Levites.
